diagnostic.root_cause: Benchmark sim loop zeroed out trajectory acceleration before passing to controller, completely nullifying feedforward capability. The GeometricTracker operated as pure PD for all 7 prior iterations despite being designed for feedforward. With feedforward activated (weight=0.4), controller anticipates turns instead of reacting to errors.
architectural_issues: Kinematic sim drag (0.5) unmodeled by controller — limits feedforward to 0.4 weight. Faessler 2018 drag compensation would enable full feedforward.
Race time still 14% above iter 5 peak (16.69s vs 14.73s) — inflation from iters 6-7 may be partially unnecessary now that feedforward is active
L-BFGS optimizer sensitive to time_weight parameter — increasing from 2.0 to 2.5 caused convergence to worse local minimum (21.6s trajectory)
Gate-4 S-turn cumulative effect still present (0.386m) though improved 24% by feedforward
critic_findings: Feedforward bug was 7 iterations old — all trajectory planning improvements (iters 5-7) were compensating for a controller at half capability
Partial feedforward (0.4) optimal due to drag mismatch — NOT a controller limitation, fixable with drag compensation
Per-gate improvements concentrated at turns (gates 3-7: -0.085 to -0.123m) with consistent benefit everywhere else
P95 tracking error improved 20% (0.682→0.543m) — tail errors reduced, not just average
Speed-accuracy Pareto frontier broken: first iteration since iter 5 where accuracy improved without sacrificing race time

improvements_backlog.description: Recover race time toward 14s target (currently 16.69s, was 14.73s at iter 5). Inflation from iters 6-7 may be reducible now that feedforward handles turns better.
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Reduce centripetal acceleration threshold from 3.5 to 4.5, or reduce inflation coefficient from 0.25 to 0.15. The feedforward controller now anticipates turns, so less pre-emptive slowing is needed.
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Race time 16.69→15.5s, avg error may increase to ~0.25m

improvements_backlog.description: Drag-compensated feedforward — full feedforward (1.0) fails due to kinematic sim drag (0.5) being unmodeled by controller
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Add drag compensation term to controller feedforward: accel_ff = ref_acc + drag_estimate * vel. This would enable higher feedforward weight (0.8-1.0) for better turn tracking.
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Avg error -10-15% further, enabling faster trajectories

improvements_backlog.description: S-turn cumulative effect — gate-4 still at 0.386m (improved 24% but still highest)
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Detect consecutive opposite-direction turns and boost inflation for the second turn, or add angular velocity reset term

improvements_backlog.description: Controller gains re-optimization with feedforward active — optimal PD gains may differ now
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Bayesian optimization of kp_xy, kd_xy, kp_z, kd_z against benchmark reward

improvements_backlog.description: PyBullet physics validation — kinematic sim results may not transfer

failed_approaches.description: Increased max_velocity from 10.0 to 12.0 AND initial time allocation from 0.6 to 0.7 simultaneously. Trajectory became too aggressive for kinematic sim PD controller — max tracking error jumped to 6.4m and gate pass rate dropped to 67%.
failed_approaches.lesson: Match trajectory aggressiveness to controller capability. Change one parameter at a time.

failed_approaches.description: Curvature-aware initial time allocation had no measurable impact because L-BFGS optimizer in _optimize_time_allocation re-optimizes times regardless of initial guess.
failed_approaches.lesson: Initial time allocation heuristic matters less than the optimizer that runs after it. Focus on optimizer constraints or objective function changes rather than initialization.
failed_approaches.metrics_delta: No measurable change in any metric

failed_approaches.description: transition_time = max(times[i], times[i+1]) for acceleration estimation at segment boundaries. Trajectory dropped to 18.1s but drone couldn't track — avg error 0.502m, race time 29.5s due to gate-seeking fallback.
failed_approaches.lesson: The acceleration estimate at segment boundaries, while rough, serves as a useful proxy for trajectory feasibility. Modifying it directly causes trajectory-tracking divergence.
failed_approaches.reason: Optimizer produced trajectories too fast for kinematic sim to follow

failed_approaches.description: transition_time = avg(times[i], times[i+1]) for acceleration estimation. Same divergence — trajectory 19.5s but only 83% gate pass rate.
failed_approaches.lesson: Both max and average transition_time variants cause the same problem. The current min() approach is the safest.
failed_approaches.reason: Still too aggressive, drone fell behind after gate-3

failed_approaches.description: time_weight = 3.0 with original acceleration estimate (max_acceleration=12). Only marginal improvement (23→21.4s) because accel penalty was still dominant.
failed_approaches.lesson: Increasing time_weight alone is insufficient — the acceleration penalty threshold (max_acceleration) must also be relaxed for meaningful speed improvement.
failed_approaches.reason: Acceleration penalty dominated objective despite higher time weight

failed_approaches.description: Adaptive symmetric entry/exit offsets (0.25-1.0m) based on turn angle. Gate-6 got 1.0m offset which pushed exit waypoint far east, away from gate-7. Race time 26.66s, avg error 0.676m.
failed_approaches.lesson: Wide offset ranges distort waypoint geometry. Gate normals don't always point toward the next gate, so large offsets along normals can push waypoints away from the ideal path.
failed_approaches.reason: Offset geometry misalignment with track layout

failed_approaches.description: Asymmetric offsets (entry 0.4-0.6m, exit 0.4-0.2m) achieved excellent gate-7 accuracy (0.271m) but race time regressed to 19-20s. Short exit offsets (0.2m) created very short through-gate segments that the L-BFGS optimizer over-slowed.
failed_approaches.lesson: Modifying entry/exit offsets has strong coupling with L-BFGS time allocation. Short segments near gate centers cause the optimizer to allocate excessive time. Better to keep offsets fixed and adjust time allocation directly.

failed_approaches.description: L-BFGS curvature-speed penalty using waypoint-level turn angles (>60° threshold). When set strong enough to improve gate-7 (0.165m), race time regressed to 20.67s. Entry/exit waypoints dilute gate-center turn angles, so the penalty threshold had to be set low, catching too many segments.
failed_approaches.lesson: Waypoint-level turn angles are much smaller than gate-center turn angles due to entry/exit point dilution. L-BFGS penalties based on waypoint angles are either ineffective (high threshold) or overly broad (low threshold). Post-optimization inflation using gate-center angles is more targeted.
failed_approaches.reason: Waypoint angle dilution makes penalty either too broad or too weak

failed_approaches.description: time_weight increased from 2.0 to 2.5 in L-BFGS optimizer. Expected faster trajectory, but optimizer converged to a worse local minimum — trajectory time jumped from 16.96s to 21.61s.
failed_approaches.lesson: The L-BFGS optimizer is sensitive to the time_weight parameter. Higher weight changes the loss landscape enough to redirect convergence. Don't assume monotonic improvement from increasing time_weight.
failed_approaches.reason: L-BFGS converged to worse local minimum
